title: What physics papers don’t tell you
abstract:
Nature Physics, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03380-7

Conventional physics publications systematically omit the failed experiments and informal collaborations that contribute to physicists’ knowledge. We propose an inverse seminar format to narrow the gap between published and actual physics.

title: Quantification of elastic barriers to rearrangement in molecular glasses
abstract:
Nature Physics, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03394-1

Elastic stresses are believed to play a role in the vitrification process in glasses, but measuring them is challenging. Imposing elastic boundary conditions is now shown to provide a way to probe elastic effects within glassy samples.

title: Rotation through sound
abstract:
Nature Physics, Published online: 30 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03384-3

Detecting quantized circulation in strongly correlated matter is challenging. Now it has been shown that phononic interferometry can reveal the quantized angular momentum of a strongly interacting rotating superfluid.

title: Long-lived phonons from resonators with reduced surface interactions
abstract:
Nature Physics, Published online: 30 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03321-4

Using Brillouin-based phonon spectroscopy, surface interactions have been identified as the dominant source of phonon decoherence in crystalline media. When these interactions are reduced through chemical mechanical polishing, high-frequency bulk acoustic wave oscillators can be realized with record Q-factors and coherence times, suitable for use as long-lived solid-state quantum memories.

title: Standards in space
abstract:
Nature Physics, Published online: 29 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03355-8

Separating long-term trends in the Earth system from instrumental drift is challenging. Yolanda Shea, Peter Pilewskie, and Rajendra Bhatt describe the push for gold-standard references in space.

title: Superconductivity with a squeeze
abstract:
Nature Physics, Published online: 28 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03393-2

Heavy-fermion superconductivity has now been observed under pressure in the van der Waals metal CeSiI. This material will provide a new platform for studying the interplay of dimensionality and Kondo physics.
